newsitem.title: USA: Texas Utils pushes Comanche restart to Fri.
newsitem.headline: Texas Utils pushes Comanche restart to Fri.

text.p: Texas Utilities Co pushed back the restart of its 1,150 Comanche Peak 2 nuclear power station to some time later today, the company said Friday.
"The plan is to restart at one p.m. (1300 CDT) today," said company spokeswoman Pat Nichols, adding it usually takes 24 to 36 hours to resume full output.
The utility said earlier this week it hoped Comanche Peak 2 would begin sending electricity to the grid Thursday.
The unit tripped off line Wednesday after a lightning strike knocked out its main feed water pump.
"It took longer to troubleshoot than expected," she said.
The adjoining Comanche Peak 1, unaffected by the Wednesday lightning storm, was operating at its 1,150 MW capacity.
The Comache Peak units, in Glen Rose, Tx., produce about 18 percent of the company's electricity deliveries.
Texas Utilities is the operator and sole owner of the Comanche Peak facility.
